title: Cursor as a Planner
shortDescription: Think of Cursor as a strategic planner that helps break down complex tasks into manageable steps and creates structured roadmaps for your projects.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can analyze your project requirements and suggest a step-by-step implementation plan
It helps you think through edge cases and potential issues before you start coding
You can ask Cursor to create task breakdowns, timelines, and architectural decisions
It acts like a project manager that understands both technical constraints and business goals

title: Cursor as a Pair Programmer
shortDescription: Cursor works alongside you like a collaborative coding partner, helping you write code, debug issues, and explore solutions together in real-time.
detailedExplanation: Cursor understands the context of your current file and entire codebase
It can suggest code completions that match your coding style and patterns
You can have back-and-forth conversations about implementation approaches
It helps you think through problems by asking clarifying questions and offering alternatives
Like a good pair programmer, it catches potential bugs and suggests improvements

title: Cursor as a Code Reviewer
shortDescription: Cursor acts as an experienced code reviewer, examining your code for bugs, style issues, performance problems, and suggesting improvements.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can review your code for common bugs, security issues, and anti-patterns
It suggests improvements for readability, maintainability, and performance
It explains why certain changes are recommended, helping you learn best practices
You can ask Cursor to review specific functions, files, or entire pull requests
It provides constructive feedback that helps you write better code over time

title: Cursor as a CI Fixer
shortDescription: When your CI pipeline fails, Cursor helps you understand the errors, fix the issues, and get your builds passing again quickly.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can read and understand CI error messages, stack traces, and test failures
It helps you identify the root cause of build failures and suggests fixes
You can paste CI logs and Cursor will help debug the specific issues
It understands different CI systems and can help with configuration issues
Cursor can help you write better tests to prevent future CI failures

title: Cursor as a Knowledge Retriever
shortDescription: Cursor acts as a smart knowledge base that can search through your codebase, documentation, and code history to find relevant information and answer questions.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can search across your entire codebase to find where specific functionality is implemented
It helps you understand how different parts of your codebase connect and interact
You can ask questions about your codebase and get answers based on actual code
It can help you discover existing patterns, utilities, and conventions in your project
Cursor remembers context from previous conversations and code you've worked on

title: Cursor as a Teacher
shortDescription: Cursor acts as an educational mentor that explains coding concepts, answers questions, and helps you learn best practices while you work.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can explain complex code patterns, algorithms, and programming concepts in simple terms
It answers your questions about how things work and why certain approaches are used
When reviewing your code, Cursor explains the reasoning behind suggestions, helping you learn
It can break down unfamiliar codebases and teach you about new frameworks or libraries
Cursor helps you understand not just what to do, but why certain solutions are better than others
